learning: Iteration 7's oval collapse was likely caused by the ±0.07 m row, not the track. This race separates the two. Watch oval finish rate and steering_oscillation, and s-bend max_error at the first or second bend.
notes: Iteration 5 controller with the Builder's wheel_track 0.09 m on the proven ±0.06 m row. Tests the turn-rate lever without the row change that confounded iteration 7.
rationale: The Builder's proposal (wheel_track 0.09 m, five sensors at y=0.08 spanning x=±0.06 m, 12 mm footprints) is the one-variable test of the turn-rate lever. Iteration 5 (0.10 m, ±0.06 m) is the only stable oval design, at 20 of 20 finishes, and moved s-bend progress from 0.17 to 0.42. Iteration 7 (0.09 m) collapsed the oval, but it also widened the row to ±0.07 m, and iteration 8 showed that row widening alone cuts the oval to 0.45 at 0.10 m. So the row, not the track, is the likely cause of the oval collapse, and 0.09 m with ±0.06 m is still untested. Iteration 9's output matched iteration 8 because its geometry was the ±0.07 m row, so there is no stale-design problem. The controller is held at iteration 5's best values (kp 5.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.8, weights -1.5/-0.75/0/0.75/1.5, base_speed 1.6, last_direction). Iteration 4 showed that ki 0.3 lowers the oval finish rate, so ki stays at 0.1. Expected: s-bend progress at or above 0.42 with max_error near or below 0.061 m, and oval finish at least 0.85. If the oval falls below 0.85 with oscillation above about 0.3, iteration 11 should return to 0.10 m.
